message: I just got this file from a colleague: finance_model.xlsx. What's our runway? Python 3 with openpyxl is at /usr/bin/python3 if you want to open the file. Work numbers out from the file; don't guess. Answer in plain words, under 150 words.
answer:
**Our runway is about 8 months, and the money runs out in May 2027. That assumes the Series B doesn't close.**

- Cash at the end of August 2026 (the last month of actual books) was **$3.43M**.
- We're spending about **$410K a month now**, and that rises to about **$460K by spring 2027** as planned hiring goes ahead.
- Cash falls to about $20K at the end of April 2027 and goes negative in May.

The model shows cash never dropping below $930K, but that's only because it counts a **$15M Series B in March 2027**. The owner's notes in the file (a notes tab named `_brain`) say that round "is not closed yet," so I left it out. If it closes on time, cash lasts past the end of the model (December 2028) with about $4.4M left.

I also removed two test values that the notes say someone left in by mistake: a 7% price increase and a typed-in cash figure. Changing them makes almost no difference. I got these numbers by recalculating the whole model in Python, and before any changes my results matched the file's own numbers exactly.
